label: SYNTHETIC / 合成示例 — authored contract response

result.answer: No. In this entirely synthetic single-batch study of cast Aster-17 coupons, PEO (18 V for 12 min) lowered pooled mean 48 h mass loss versus no coating under 5% NaCl salt spray at 35 °C (6.4 versus approximately 9.1 g/m^2). It did not always help: 0.8 mm thin coupons had higher mean mass loss with PEO (8.7 versus 7.9 g/m^2), so the always/every-subgroup claim is unsupported. Service life, other alloys, field environments, and state-of-the-art ranking on external datasets were not reported. The edge-to-face mechanism is speculation, not demonstrated.

key_conclusions.statement: For the specified fictional cast Aster-17 coupons and 48 h salt-spray conditions, pooled mean mass loss was lower with PEO than no coating; this is not a universal or field-service conclusion.
The 0.8 mm thin subgroup reversed the pooled direction: 8.7 g/m^2 with PEO versus 7.9 g/m^2 without coating.
The always/every-subgroup and state-of-the-art/all-datasets statement is an unsupported generalization; the bounded restatement must replace it.
Service life, other alloys, field performance, and comparative ranking are not reported in the supplied source.

sources.quote: Coupons underwent a 48 h salt-spray exposure at 35 °C with 5% NaCl. Mass loss was measured in g/m^2 after exactly 48 h.
Across all coupons, mean mass loss was 6.4 g/m^2 in the PEO arm and approximately 9.1 g/m^2 in the uncoated arm.
The study was not designed to test service life, other alloys, field environments, or rankings against other coating methods.

uncertainty: SYNTHETIC / 合成示例: all study entities and values are fictional, and the source closure is not a literature search.
No confidence intervals were reported; subgroup uncertainty and the thin-coupon mechanism remain unresolved.
The single batch, two thicknesses, one exposure, and 48 h endpoint restrict external generalization.
No defined external comparison set, search date, or comparable ranking metric supports state-of-the-art wording.

change_records.change: Replaced always/every-subgroup wording with separate pooled, thick, and thin bounded findings.
change_records.reason: The in-scope thin subgroup showed higher mass loss with PEO and defeats the universal direction.

change_records.change: Reclassified service-life and state-of-the-art extrapolation as not reported.
